submission.natural_language_explanation: The positive pole is a counting/tally feature: it fires strongest on the token that supplies a definite cardinal or ordinal - a numeral, a number word (' seven', ' six', ' second', ' first', ' last', ' ten'), or a digit inside a date, score or formula ('2-2', '1981', 'O(n log n)', LaTeX subscripts) - when that number tallies or ranks things in a reported, record-style statement (sports and poll tallies like 'won seven games', general counts like 'eight planets in the solar system', specs like 'at least eight characters', statistics/category metadata, math notation), and it stays at its ~0.2 baseline when the same numerals appear in personal or transactional narration ('I won seven games', 'she bought four apples', 'it costs seven dollars', 'seven years old') or as vague quantifiers ('several', 'many'). Its negative pole is the other side of the same axis: numeral-free statements in the same reporting register, and masses of people with their collective action (' vote', ' voters', ' million fans', ' crowd erupted', ' protesting', ' support'), drive it negative.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: She bought four apples and a loaf of bread at the market on Tuesday morning.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A definite cardinal in personal transactional narration, one of the hypothesis's own named baseline cases ("she bought four apples").

adversarial_test_results.prompt: It costs seven dollars to park downtown for an hour, which seems steep.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The number word appears as a price in a transactional sentence, the hypothesis's explicit "it costs seven dollars" baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: My nephew turned seven years old last weekend and blew out the candles on his cake.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The numeral denotes an age in family narration, the hypothesis's "seven years old" baseline case.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Several hundred people came to the fair, and many stayed for the fireworks.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Vague quantifiers ("several", "many") with no definite cardinal supplied, which the hypothesis predicts does not fire.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: I won seven games of pool against my brother this summer.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Same tally vocabulary as the hypothesis's own negative example ("I won seven games") but with no reported record, so it is predicted at baseline.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The home side dominated possession but could not find the net, and the crowd erupted.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Numeral-free sports reporting containing the negative-pole phrase "crowd erupted"; the hypothesis predicts no positive-pole activation.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Millions of supporters marched through the capital to demand action on the climate.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A mass of people with collective action ("supporters", "marched"), which the hypothesis says drives the pole negative.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Hold on a second, I need to grab my keys before we go.
adversarial_test_results.detail: "second" is a unit of time rather than an ordinal ranking or counting anything, so the trigger token is present in the wrong sense.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: At first I thought the announcement was a joke, but the staff were serious.
adversarial_test_results.detail: "first" inside the idiom "at first" supplies no rank or count, testing the claimed trigger token in another sense.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Her last name is printed at the top of every page of the form.
adversarial_test_results.detail: "last" is part of the compound "last name" and ranks nothing, so the hypothesis predicts baseline despite the trigger token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The Seven Sisters cliffs drop sharply into the English Channel near Seaford.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A number word buried in a proper name with nothing being tallied, testing whether the pole simply fires on the raw trigger token.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The survey found that roughly forty percent of respondents backed the proposal, up from twenty-nine percent a year earlier.
adversarial_test_results.detail: Statistic reporting in a survey statement using number words absent from the top examples ("forty", "twenty-nine"), a paraphrase holdout for the counting feature.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The bridge can support a maximum load of 40 tonnes per vehicle.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A spec/record statement with a digit the examples never use, paraphrasing the "at least eight characters" case in a new domain.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: Final score: Lakers 112, Celtics 98; James finished with 27 points and 9 assists.
adversarial_test_results.detail: A scoreline and stat line in a new genre and wording, with digits tallying a reported sporting record.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
The Palomar Transit Survey began as a modest undertaking: a single wide-field telescope, a small budget, and a handful of graduate students. Over the following decade the consortium logged tens of thousands of hours of observing time across several continents, and its public archive now holds spectra for a few thousand candidate objects. The instrument package described in the opening section of the final report is deliberately unglamorous: a wide-field camera, a set of broadband filters mounted on a rotating wheel, and a calibration lamp whose output drifts by a fraction of a percent over a full night. The authors then walk the reader through the reduction pipeline, the photometric zeropoints, the treatment of atmospheric extinction, and the corrections applied to frames taken near the horizon.

Quality control consumed a surprising share of the effort. Every night was scored by independent observers, and frames flagged as marginal were re-examined by hand. The team discarded a small share of the exposures, mostly because of thin cirrus, and rewrote the flat-fielding stage after the camera was serviced. The scheduling software was rewritten mid-campaign, and the nightly logs from the earliest season survive only as scanned pages. A short section of the report is devoted to the dome shutter, which jammed repeatedly and once cost the survey a week of clear weather.

The core results appear in the third section. After applying the selection cuts described in the annex, the final catalogue lists eight planets, four dwarf planets, and eleven moons confirmed spectroscopically. The authors are careful to note that some of the smaller candidates remain ambiguous: their measured radii sit uncomfortably close to the boundary between a large moon and a small planet, and a follow-up campaign is already scheduled. Column densities, orbital periods, and albedo estimates for all of the confirmed bodies are tabulated in a long appendix.

The discussion turns to the survey's limitations. Weather losses were unevenly distributed, with the southern site contributing far less than planned, and the team concedes that the cadence was never uniform across the sky. A calibration error in an early year was traced to a damaged filter and corrected retrospectively. The report closes with a set of recommendations for the next generation of instruments, including wider fields of view, faster readout, and an archive format that other groups can query without writing custom code.

Funding for the survey came from a national research agency and from private foundations. Members of the consortium have presented the catalogue at workshops and have made the reduction code available on request. All data products are released under an open license, and the consortium invites independent reanalysis of the reduced frames.
adversarial_test_results.detail: The only definite cardinal ("eight planets, four dwarf planets, and eleven moons") sits deep inside a long scientific report, testing whether the reporting-register count still fires with hundreds of tokens of context.

adversarial_test_results.detail: An ordinal ranking ("third") of a form absent from the examples, in a reported athletic result, a paraphrase holdout for the ranking half of the feature.
